story.title: A precise failure case reduced unnecessary exploration
story.problem: Synthetic example. A bounded knowledge-work task produced a plausible first answer, but the result needed repeated corrections. The objective was to improve the usable outcome without hiding errors or relying on a more impressive-looking response. Inputs and acceptance criteria were fixed for this invented comparison.
story.change: The fictional contributor replaced a broad debugging request with a reproducible failure and explicit acceptance checks. The agent still had room to investigate, but each proposed fix had to explain and resolve the same failure.
story.result: In this invented comparison, the token index moved from 100 to 75 while the same quality checks passed. The rounded index illustrates a possible result format; it does not establish real savings or subscription cost reduction.
story.lesson: Before asking for a broad investigation, identify one observable failure and how success will be checked. Test whether this focuses exploration without concealing a wider defect.
story.limits: All events and numbers are fictional demonstrations of the reporting format. They are not customer evidence or a completed benchmark. A future real comparison must retain every trial, record model and evaluator conditions, and examine unseen tasks. This story is excluded from rankings, progress awards, and candidate discovery.
